version: Learning-focused gameplay v12: positive weights, effort forecasts, peer scoring practice and continuous escalation

checks: Every possible integer split preserves total 100, range 1–98 and deterministic effort
Either remaining card confirms the pair after any first-card choice
Both equal remaining sliders can move in either direction before confirmation
Available bounds clamp safely, reserving one percent, without changing locked weights or snapshots
Near-even accepts gaps through 10 points inclusively, rejects 11, and produces three medium shots
Run requires all three confirmed weights (including the linked pair) and a valid complete allocation
The second experiment requires a changed split and never forces a direction or degree of balance
All 20 trios retain single, tied and near-even highest observed effort independently of all seven forecast subsets
Copied runs, partner requests and compared snapshots independently copy predictions as well as weights and metrics
Every six-metric branch supplies three peer-action beats with an unresolved content question; other scenes keep their existing contracts
Keyboard and native slider bounds reserve at least 1%; 98/1/1 and 61/38/1 remain valid, with either final confirmation locking the pair
Forecasts require a deliberate selection, allow toggling and keyboard input, reset on re-entry and compare against tied actual effort without a correctness reward
Replay preserves the recorded forecast and satisfaction; a fresh near-even prediction can select all three, and both actual tests reach comparison
balance-check stays explicit, asks for its own forecast and retains both player tests alongside the reference
contrast-check stays explicit, asks for its own forecast and retains both player tests alongside the reference
The six-metric scene visibly shares and copies a scoring phrase, lets the classmate ask a content question and leaves it open while both collect ticks
One growth action passes 10/25/100 and each satisfaction checkpoint; hidden time holds, no repeated Add button is needed and the final classroom observation still waits for a click
768px forecasts, result markers and peer scene fit without horizontal overflow; phone portraits remain clear of the phrase cards
390px forecasts, result markers and peer scene fit without horizontal overflow; phone portraits remain clear of the phrase cards
320px forecasts, result markers and peer scene fit without horizontal overflow; phone portraits remain clear of the phrase cards
No runtime errors in offline forecasts, positive-weight extremes, reference routes, social scene or continuous growth
All four latest ZIPs are intact, self-contained and byte-identical to their production builds and manifest
The review ZIP contains separate Level 3 and connected Levels 1–3 HTMLs, identical to their tested latest packages
Packaged Level2.html completes 3 → 6 → 10 → 25 → 100 offline with normal motion
Packaged standalone Level3.html completes both weight tests and compares the actual results offline
Packaged Level1.html includes the latest behaviour and two replies, stops after Level 1 and permits replay
Standalone Level 1 reload starts a fresh Level 1 run
Packaged combined game continues from the current Level 1 into playable Level 2 and keeps sound preference
Packaged combined game connects Level 1 → Level 2 → playable Level 3 in one open run
Combined preview reload starts from Level 1 rather than restoring Level 2
Packaged entries have no browser runtime errors
Opening-supplied player name reaches Level 3 labels, avatar and the three weighted partner shots
Level 3 completes once with immutable tested runs and an explicit near-even/uneven comparison payload
Comparison leads to theory; even duplicate final callbacks stay in the placeholder and never invoke Design Lab
Real Gameplay host carries the opening name and sound preference from Level 2 into the new Level 3 chapter
Level 3 preselects the actual Level 2 trio, permits swapping, and has no player Restart control
Reloading the connected host starts fresh from its configured entry level
Hidden-page publication holds its visible-time sequence and resumes without skipping the three weights
Real-time publication and evidence arrive one at a time; Web Audio cues play and Sound off silences later updates
No browser errors in partner, chapter handoff or real-time audio checks
All gameplay emoji are distinct across all levels
Every valid integer split uses the 10-point near-even boundary and the correct one/two higher-reward family
All 20 trios have concise pattern-specific reviews; near-even exposes the scoring stopping rule
Second-result questions describe actual increases, decreases and unchanged effort bands
Both comparison orders and both system references describe the latest actual pattern without assuming an improvement
No dialogue or emoji repeats within 8,640 complete trial paths, including repeated patterns and unchanged scene intensity
Six Level 1 review questions and all 20 Level 2 trio exchanges differ; player names remain supplied text

notes: Minimum weight is 1%; all valid positive integer triples and slider/confirmation bounds were checked. Publication rejects zero weights, including the reported 61/39/0 case. Its available endpoint is 61/38/1; the overall maximum is 98/1/1.

Every player test and explicit system reference requests a deliberate one-or-more-card forecast. Results retain that forecast alongside the actual qualitative effort, including tied highest bands. Back/re-entry clears an unsubmitted forecast; replays preserve the recorded forecast. Predictions never alter effort or satisfaction.

All 20 trios, six qualitative patterns and seven forecast subsets were checked for highest effort independent of the prediction. Predicted metric arrays are independently copied in partner requests, compared runs and completion snapshots.

The six-metric placeholder visibly shares a scoring phrase, shows a classmate copying and questioning it, then returns both students to collecting ticks while the content question remains open. The optional peerInteraction payload supplies three text/action beats for finished partner animations.

One Add more metrics action now advances through 10/25/100 with short illustrated actions. Tests observed every satisfaction checkpoint (70/77/82/86), verified hidden-page holding and retained the explicit Observe action at 100.

47 focused rule, forecast/peer-contract, offline-browser, dialogue, partner and actual-package checks passed on the final builds. Forecast/result and peer scenes fit 768/390/320px in the production checks; the desktop flows and screenshots were also inspected.

All five latest ZIPs have CRC/hash integrity checks and HTML identical to their production builds. The review ZIP contains the same standalone Level 3 and connected full-game HTML as the individual packages.
The v11 baseline is preserved on archive/pre-learning-optimizations-v11 at fc279fc38c2a8ce4d913317b4f2102fae44d78c8. Older archive branches and historical versioned ZIPs remain unchanged.

Opening animation integration and the Level 1 opening transition were intentionally not changed in this gameplay-only step. The existing final theory-placeholder endpoint still does not enter Design Lab.

Functional checks do not establish measured learning effectiveness. Offline checks use exact production/packaged HTML on an in-memory HTTPS origin; direct file opening in the user’s browser, classroom load capacity and finished video assets are not claimed as tested. Earlier broader suites remain historical in their versioned reports and were not rerun in full.
